items.name: BFS Cycle Detection with Generation Counter
items.symbol: check_noncircular(src, target), circular_queue, dep_gen_id generation counter, __bfs_forwards()
items.counter_case: Cortex's entity graph is small (<200 entities); O(n) DFS is negligible. The generation counter optimization is premature at this scale.

items.name: DECLARE_EWMA Type-Safe Adaptive Compaction Pressure
items.counter_case: EWMA adds temporal hysteresis. A one-time large ingest would keep threshold elevated for many subsequent operations, causing under-compaction until the EWMA forgets the spike.

items.name: Bounded Event Queue + IN_Q_OVERFLOW Sentinel
items.counter_case: An overflow event requires the consumer to do a full re-scan, which may be more expensive than processing the individual events.

items.name: cortex.json Schema Bounds Validation (min/max per tunable)
items.counter_case: Runtime validation duplicates JSON Schema min/maximum keywords. Better to use JSON Schema for validation than hand-coded bounds.

items.name: Scanned/Reclaimed Miss-Ratio to 3-Level Pressure Signal
items.counter_case: Cold-start Cortex has 100% miss rate (empty cache). Window would immediately fire CRITICAL. Requires warm-up guard of minimum N lookups before pressure is computed.

items.name: Shadow Entry + Refault Distance for Skeleton Cache
items.counter_case: Shadow entry bookkeeping requires a separate Map growing proportionally to evicted entities. At Cortex's scale the added complexity may not be worth it.

items.name: Adaptive Context-Pack Window: get_next_ra_size Ramp
items.symbol: get_next_ra_size(ra, max): cur<max/16->4x, cur<=max/2->2x, else max
items.counter_case: LLM access patterns are rarely sequential. Window would expand, pre-fetch wrong entities, and waste ingest budget. Must gate on confirmed sequential pattern (>=3 sequential accesses).

items.name: Sequence Cookie Async with Domain Isolation
items.symbol: async_cookie_t, async_synchronize_cookie_domain(), async_domain, MAX_WORK graceful-sync fallback
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded; synchronize_cookie() becomes a Promise chain — which is just Promise.all() with extra steps at this scale.

items.name: Two-Tier CLOCK (inactive/active) for Skeleton Cache
items.symbol: Double CLOCK lists: inactive (fault in here) + active (promoted on 2nd access); demotion when active grows
items.counter_case: The two-tier cache adds promotion/demotion bookkeeping. At <5000 entities the LRU walk (C2 from prior audit) already covers this use case.

items.name: XArray Mark Bits vs JavaScript Map for Dirty Entity Tracking
items.cortex_advantage: JavaScript Map with separate dirty Set sufficient for <5000 entities; XArray overkill
items.steel_man: XArray mark bits propagate upward — O(log n) find-next-dirty vs O(n) Map filter; eliminates separate dirty Set at scale

items.name: SLUB 3-Tier Per-CPU Cache Hierarchy
items.violated_principle: Local-first: per-CPU partitioning requires OS preemption model absent in Node.js single-threaded event loop

items.name: Lazy fsnotify_set_children_dentry_flags Propagation
items.symbol: DCACHE_FSNOTIFY_PARENT_WATCHED flag, lazy clear in fsnotify_clear_child_dentry_flag()
items.violated_principle: Domain mismatch at scale: Cortex watches O(10) directories, not O(millions) of dentries; eager flag setting costs nothing

items.name: Unchecked Integer Arithmetic in Token/Score Accumulation
items.symbol: check_add_overflow(a, b, d), wrapping_add(type, a, b) — model of explicit overflow handling
items.pattern: Token counts and savings ledger sums use bare + arithmetic without Number.isSafeInteger() guard. Silent precision loss if count approaches 2^53.
items.proposed_action: Add CLAUDE.md rule: any counter accumulating over time must use Number.isSafeInteger() assertion or BigInt. Add scripts/check-unsafe-arithmetic.ts CI grep.
items.why_target_chose_it: The kernel cannot afford silent integer overflow; every arithmetic operation on counters uses explicit overflow-checked variants

items.name: Two-Tier CLOCK vs 6-State LRU Walk: Which Policy for Skeleton Cache?
items.question: Should Cortex implement the two-tier CLOCK macro-policy (C14) alongside the 6-state per-item callback (C2 from prior audit), or pick one?
alternatives: Two-tier CLOCK only (C14): simpler, matches Linux page cache, good for LLM access patterns where 2nd access = hot signal
6-state callback only (C2): more flexible, individual entities veto/rotate their own eviction
Both together: Linux actually uses both — two tiers as macro policy, 6-state callback as micro policy within the inactive list eviction walk

items.name: At What Lookup Volume Does the Miss-Ratio Window Produce Meaningful Signal?
items.question: What should CORTEX_PRESSURE_WIN be? The window must smooth noise but respond quickly enough to be useful.
alternatives: Fixed window of 50 entity lookups: small, responsive, noisy for cold start
Exponential: start at 10, double on each pressure event up to 500 (adapts to workload intensity)
Time-based: compute ratio over last 60 seconds (ignores burst vs idle trade-off)
